- [USER] User expressed interest in the differences between the Amish faith and other Anabaptist groups.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Amish lifestyle and culture are distinct and traditional, involving traditional clothing, tight-knit farming communities, and simple churches.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amish communities generally shun modern technology, unlike other Anabaptist groups such as Mennonites who may use cars, tractors, and even computers and smartphones.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Amish require adult baptism for church membership, while other Anabaptist groups may baptize children or infants.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Amish practice shunning or excommunication more strictly than other Anabaptist groups.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amish education typically occurs in small, one-room schoolhouses, while other Anabaptist groups may use public or private schools.
- [USER] User found it interesting that the Amish faith emphasizes community and rejection of modern technology.
- [USER] User inquired if other Anabaptist groups also prioritize community and rejection of modern technology.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other Anabaptist groups, like Mennonites, also prioritize community and service, with close-knit congregations and sustainable agricultural practices.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Hutterites live communally and reject modern technology, while Bruderhof communities prioritize communal living but allow some modern technology.
- [USER] User expressed admiration for how Anabaptist groups balance tradition and modernity and asked for specific examples or stories.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mennonite and other Anabaptist communities prioritize sustainable living practices, such as organic farming and renewable energy sources.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Anabaptist communities run successful businesses, such as furniture making and produce farming, to integrate with the outside world while maintaining their values.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many Mennonite churches advocate for social justice causes, supporting refugees and addressing climate change while emphasizing community and simplicity.
